title: A narrative states each figure in the role its input holds, or as a quoted text holds it
assertion: Passes: days, pages, versions, releases, levels, years, counts, units and rows each with their words, in digits, with commas or in words; a quoted figure beside its own words, in the role its quote gives it; at least 100 hand-written forms not drawn from the drafting templates; each figure in the role of the noun after it or its nearest cue (“the $30.00 difference”, “the payer paid the contract rate”, a deadline after “days after payment”), “respectively” in order in its two plain forms, its cues right before the list (“The contract expected per line and the payer allowed per line $100.00 and $70.00, respectively”) or right after it (“$100.00 and $70.00 were the expected and allowed amounts per line, respectively”, “$100.00 and $70.00, respectively, were ...”), each figure in the scope phrase right after its cue (“$300.00 and $70.00 were expected in total and allowed per line, respectively”), else the whole list’s (right after the list, or right after “amounts”), never a clause after “respectively”; an amount with a scope phrase of the closed list beside it, right after it (“per line”, “a line”, “for each line”, “on each of the 3 lines”, “in total”, “in all”, “across the 3 lines”, “for all the lines”, “for the claim” where the pattern has one claim) or right before it (“each line’s”, “the per-line”, “a total of”); an earlier clause’s figure beside a “respectively” list as its own (“The payer paid $56.00 per line, while $100.00 and $70.00 were the expected and allowed amounts per line, respectively”); an amount with no scope, or in a sentence that names a part of the lines, where its role’s per-line and total values are one; each line’s and the lines’ totals, ordinals and partitives as prose (“the first 3 claims”, “2 of the 3 claims”), “Lines 1–3”, a locked fee schedule’s year and business days to pay; a number with no role fails
noFileReason: Narratives against the SYNTHETIC packets of @tp/packets/testing (role-examples.ts): no file.
